claims.statement: For n>=3, a strict cross-majority partition implies lambda2(H)>=2/(n-1), with equality exactly for K1 join (Km disjoint union Km).
assumptions: every cross degree strictly greater than half the opposite part
claims.novelty: No exact match located in bounded search; no priority certification.

claims.statement: For connected H and a fixed partition, a positive z with tau=min_u (Cz)_u/(d_u z_u)>=0 gives lambda2(H)>=(2+tau)/(n-1). The best tau is the smallest generalized eigenvalue of (C,D).
assumptions: C is the defined missing-cross-pair matrix
claims.novelty: Matrix equivalence, ground-state transformation and positive-vector optimization are classical; graph-specific consequence distinguished.

claims.statement: For every k>=4, Kkk minus k-2 edges at one vertex has no strict-majority or strict-minority partition, but an explicit integer weighted witness proves lambda2 >= (k^2+2k-5)/((4k-7)(2k-1)) > 1/8.
claims.novelty: Strict certificate-class enlargement; the explicit family spectrum is elementary and is not claimed inaccessible to existing methods.

claims.statement: A strict-majority partition with both parts at least two has an explicit parity-dependent positive surplus and, in particular, lambda2>=2/(n-1)+1/(2(n-1)^2(n-2)).
claims.novelty: Quantitative exclusion of equality within the class, not edit-distance stability.

claims.statement: The stated quadratic-form condition on a connected base graph is equivalent to its one-leaf extension having normalized gap at least 2/N.
assumptions: degree-weighted centering and exact stated coefficient
claims.novelty: Exact application of standard elimination; elementary complete-bipartite spectrum presented proportionately.
